chapter: MJQ, Pettiford and the move to Paris
title: Phineas Newborn trio at Basin Street; Michel Legrand's invitation to Paris
summary: Seeing Michel Legrand on TV, Clarke phoned him; Legrand sat in at Basin Street and offered a place in his uncle's jazz orchestra, so Clarke moved to Paris in September 1956.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: -- I began to work with Phineas Newborn, Oscar and I, you know.
And we began to work with Phineas and -- in Basin Street.

So one night -- no, one afternoon, I happened to turn the TV on, and I saw a guy -- how things work -- with a white suit on, with his back turned, directing the band, and he's shaking his buns and carrying on, so I said, "I know that guy. I know him." So when he turned around it was a Maurice Chevalier spectacular, with Michel Legrand directing the orchestra. So when I turned around, I said, "That's Michel." So I went to the phone and I called CBS, backstage, and I said, "This is Kenny Clarke, I'd like to speak to Michel Legrand, it's very important." Said, "Just a moment, Kenny, I'll call him." So Michel came to the phone. He said, "Hey, Kenny, how are you?" I said, "Oh, I'm fine. I just saw you on TV. I just wanted to let you know that you were wonderful," and so forth and so on. He says, "Well, are you working in New York?" I said, "Yeah, we're working at the Basin Street." He says, "Where is that?" I said, "Right around the corner, on Broadway and 51st Street." He said, "I'll be there tonight." So he comes at night and he sits in, he loves Phineas, and we began to have

a lot of fun. He was singing and having fun. So just before he left he says, "Listen, would you like to come back to Paris?" I said, "I would love nothing better." He said, "Well, my uncle Henan Jacques Eliam (PHONETIC), is forming an orchestra. He's going to play nothing but jazz." So I said, "Wonderful." He says, "Will you give me your word?" I said, "Yeah, you have my word, Michel." So he left. Two weeks later I had a contract from his uncle, and that was like in August, in September I was gone. I came back in --
September, '56. I came to Paris, and that was it.
It was evidently meant to be, I guess. Wasn't it?
You know, I guess so, yeah. Yeah.
